title: Long Page Number with Title on First Page

illustrates.quote: A blank line is not inserted between the alphabetic page number and the full title on the first page of text.

page.features: First page of text: alphabetic page number spanning two braille lines, followed immediately (no blank line) by the title and subtitle. Numeric page number '#acge' decodes to 1375 (a=1,c=3,g=7,e=5).

blocks.features: Alphabetic (spelled-out) form of the numeric print page number 1,375 ('one-thousand three hundred seventy-five'), split across braille lines 1-2.
Placeholder book title on the first page of text, immediately following the page number with no intervening blank line, per 1.14.1.g.
Placeholder subtitle line beneath the title.

braille.notes: Braille page lines 1-4, line 1-2 reconstructed to 40 cells each (same raw-extraction artefact as example-1-7/14/15). Lines 1-2 carry the long alphabetic page number, preceded by six cells of the page-change-indicator symbol and ending with the numeric page number 1375 ('#acge': a=1,c=3,g=7,e=5) at the end of line 1, with the runover ('seventy-five') beginning in cell 7 of line 2, per 1.14.1.c. Line 3 (the placeholder title) follows immediately with NO intervening blank line, per 1.14.1.g (the rule this example illustrates); line 4 the placeholder subtitle.

resolution: Both runs agree on the braille content and on there being no real print excerpt to build from. Emboss has no spelled-out (alphabetic) page-number feature at all (standards-findings.md F-49) -- there is also no real print content behind the placeholder. status: not-representable (limitation: no print given, and F-49).
